5.2 If your Customer Service Standard performance falls below the agreed standards, this will be discussed with your Performance Manager during performance reviews and improvement action agreed as part of the Performance Management Intervention Regime.

Funding model

5.3 There are 2 distinct elements to the Confident Futures funding model:

Delivery Fee

Output Payment

Delivery Fee Payment

5.4 Delivery Fee will constitute 80% of the total contract value. You will not need to submit claims for Delivery Fee payments. The Delivery Fee will be automatically paid to you monthly in arrears from month one of the contract going live, up to and including month 20.

Output Payment

5.5 Output payments are capped at 20% of the total contract value. You will only be paid an Output Payment when DWP has confirmed that the qualifying conditions described in the Confident Futures Specification and later in this section have been met.

Qualifying conditions for Output Payments

5.6 Output payments are only payable where the agreed Output has been completed in accordance with the requirements set out in the Specification (Annex 8: Submission Timings and Acceptance Criteria) and submitted within the required timescales.

5.7 Providers must submit completed Outputs within the timescales set out in the Specification (Annex 8 Submission Timings and Acceptance Criteria) and Chapter 9: Confident Futures Contract Metrics, Managing Performance and Risk Assurance of this Guidance. The Authority will review all submitted Outputs and, where an Output does not meet the required standards or further information is required, may request that the provider rework and resubmit the Output. Outputs submitted outside the required timescales, or which do not meet the required quality standards, are incomplete, or are not supported by sufficient evidence following any rework and resubmission request, will be deemed ineligible for payment.

5.8 All submissions will be assessed by the Authority, and payment will only be made where the qualifying conditions have been met.

Payments to providers

5.9 All payments will be made through the appropriate IT system or PRaP in line with the amounts set out in the contract. Note that DWP can only make direct payments to UK bank accounts.

5.10 When shipping Management information (MI) lines these will appear as outcome payments of £0.01 each, note these payments will be made on the next working day. Details of these payments are described in Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referral and Payment (PRaP) System for Confident Futures in the MI lines.

VAT

5.11 Your VAT obligations are covered in the Terms and Conditions of the contract.

Additional VAT Requirements for Self-billing Contracts

5.12 The following guidance should be read in conjunction with the HMRC guidance VAT Notice 700/62: Self-Billing.

5.13 HMRC guidance states that under a self-billing contract both parties are responsible for ensuring that the VAT is charged correctly on invoices. As part of your bid, you were asked to provide the VAT rate or rates that should be charged for each part of the funding model.

Note: You will be asked to confirm that the VAT rate or rates quoted as part of your bid are still correct prior to commencement date of the contract. The onus is on you to provide the VAT rate for this contract as per HMRC guidelines. DWP will however, assist in this matter by providing an annual self-billing contract and requesting confirmation of the VAT rate or rates. If the self-billing agreement process is delayed for any reason, you are still responsible for notifying the VAT rate or rates to the Authority on an annual basis.

DWP’s responsibilities

5.14 DWP is responsible for ensuring that:

VAT rates are sent to the provider

an annual self-billing agreement is in place; and VAT rate or rates are changed on the PRaP system if you notify a change in your VAT status

5.15 DWP will seek agreement from you to the self-billing arrangement on an annual basis and request that you confirm the VAT rate or rates to be applied to all aspects of the funding model.

Provider’s responsibilities

5.16 You are responsible for:

providing a signed self-billing agreement promptly on an annual basis when requested by DWP

ensuring that DWP is immediately notified of a change in the VAT rate(s) should they change during an agreement term

ensuring that duplicate invoices are not sent to DWP for a supply which is self-billed

ensuring that you fully understand and comply with VAT Notice 700/62

Chapter 6: Health and safety, accidents, unacceptable behaviour, fraud prevention and complaints

6.1 This chapter pulls together various key pieces of information that you will need to be aware of in respect of working with your Participants and also details what you must have in place to ensure Participants who are unhappy with the service they receive are able to raise a confidential complaint, and the processes you must follow to respond and resolve any issues raised.

Health and safety

6.2 All Participants on Confident Futures are entitled to train and work in a healthy and safe environment with due regard to their welfare. Under Health and Safety Law they are regarded as your employees, whether they are paid by you or not. You must, therefore, comply with your Duty of Care under the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 and the Act’s associated regulations in the same way as you would do for any other member of your workforce.

6.3 You must ensure that your Participants receive appropriate health and safety induction, training and supervision, and that systems are in place for checking this, both within your own organisation and at any of your supply chain partners.

3.186 All breaks in support and discussions concerning them must be recorded in the Support Plan.

Chapter 3h: In-Work Support (IWS) on Confident Futures

3.187 IWS will be provided to Participants who move into employment. For those Participants entering work, and with their consent, you should, complete an Employment Support Plan (ESP) and issue it to the employer within 10 working days of the Participant entering Employment or self-employment.

3.188 IWS will be in place for either the remainder of the Participants time on the programme (up to 365 days from their start date) or until the they no longer require it.

3.189 In the rare event where a Participant does not agree to an ESP being produced, you must ensure this decision is clearly documented, dated, and formally recorded in their Support Plan. Supporting evidence should also be retained to support compliance and assurance activities. If the Participant wants to remain on the programme you should continue to provide tailored IWS to them and continue to update their Support Plan.

3.190 If a Participant moves into employment, remind the Participant to notify their PTWA as per Chapter 3e: Change of Circumstances while on Confident Futures. They may decide they do not require IWS, and they can choose to end their participation in the programme at this point. Refer to Chapter 4: Leaving Confident Futures and Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referral and Payment (PRaP) System for Confident Futures for action to take for completers in this scenario.

Note: You should not request the Participant to notify the PTWA if they are not in receipt of Universal Credit.

3.191 You will be responsible for the design of the ESP which must set out the support you will give to the Participant and the employer during the IWS period, for the duration of the programme (up to 365 calendar days), to help the Participant sustain employment. It will also include the Participant’s support needs from the employer after you are no longer involved, after the period of IWS. The ESP should contain as a minimum:

a description of the IWS you are providing to the Participant

any actions required of the Participant in relation to the IWS

all Non-Confident Futures Activities

3.192 You must provide tailored IWS to both the Participant and the employer to help the Participant stay in work, except where the Participant has stated they do not require it. The IWS should be provided by the same Dedicated Adviser, and to the same frequency and intensity as during the pre-employment support phase.

3.193 The same level of support will be expected for those Participants who choose to become self-employed. It is not intended that you would act in a small business advisor capacity, rather you should continue to support the Participant with on-going management of their barriers to work as you would with an employed Participant. You should signpost the Participant towards agencies that can support them with appropriate business advice, including helping the Participant to access the Access to Work (AtW) provision.

3.194 Support for each Participant must include, but is not limited to:

maintaining frequency of contact (at least once every 4 calendar weeks) with Participant, with any additional contact as required

where appropriate, the Participant being accompanied to the workplace by the Dedicated Adviser, and the Dedicated Adviser supporting the Participant in meetings with the Participant’s line manager and colleagues

on-going engagement with the Participant’s wider sustainable support network (both formal and informal networks)

practical actions, for example socialising and integration in the work environment, journey planning, pre-start visits for familiarisation, establishing a buddy in the workplace

facilitating any reasonable adjustments required and where appropriate, ensuring Access to Work (AtW) assistance is in place from the from the start of employment

3.195 The ESP must be updated when the Participant enters employment or self-employment and at least every 4 calendar weeks throughout IWS. Where Participant has stated they do not want an ESP, you should update the Support Plan.

3.196 Check the possible impact on the Participant’s welfare benefits of any paid employment undertaken and ensure these are understood by the Participant.

Confident Futures employer support offer

3.197 You will be expected to have and to build strong links to national and local employers, helping to build disability confidence and to increase the capacity and sustainability of employers including Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) to recruit and retain disabled people.

3.198 You must provide a full employer support offer focussed on working with the employer so that the employer can continue to support the Participant in work after the provision has ended. The employer support offer will include meeting with employers and their staff and encouraging employers to find champions/advocates within their workplace. This will also involve up-skilling employers and developing a support network that will continue to work together to meet the Participant’s needs and help them to sustain employment.

3.199 You have a role in developing the confidence of the employers you work with in the delivery of the Provision to accommodate disabled people in their workplace and to understand the principles of “Disability Confident”. This includes increasing an employer’s disability awareness and capability. You will need to ensure that employers are able to continue to support each Participant with their support network and AtW where appropriate once the delivery of IWS on Confident Futures ends.

Local tailoring and stakeholder engagement

DWP IT Systems Provider Referrals and Payments (PRaP) User Guidance, and

DWP Supplier Code of Conduct

1.20 This guidance provides additional information to the schedules of your contract(s). provider guidance does not look to replicate or replace the details within your contract, and you are responsible for ensuring you read, understand and are complying with your contract.

1.21 You must ensure that any organisations with which you have a sub-contractual relationship also have access to, and have read, the Confident Future’s provider guidance.

1.22 If you have any questions which are not covered by this guidance, raise with your Employment Account Division Performance Manager (EAD PM) in the first instance.

Document retention

1.23 Providers must maintain complete documents and records in relation to Confident Futures for the period of their contract. The contract Terms & Conditions will set out the relevant contract periods and the Records Retention End Date.

Welsh Language Act

1.24 Providers are reminded of the need to comply with the provisions of Schedule 16 (Welsh Language) in providing the Services in the Welsh language. This must apply to all your staff and supply chain.

1.25 Details will be in the relevant schedules as set out within your contract.

The Employment Provision Provider Code of Conduct (“Code”)

1.26 The Code outlines the standards and behaviours that the government expects of all its providers when they are working with government, and how providers can help the government deliver for taxpayers.

1.27 Providers that contract with the DWP will be expected to operate in accordance with the Code. The Code can be found at Schedule 14 of the Confident Futures Agreement.

Obtaining a Participant signature

1.28 When obtaining a Participant’s signature, Confident Futures is not prescriptive about how the signature is obtained. You have the option to use one (or more) robust digital alternatives to obtain and store a Participant’s signature as part of the evidence of activities undertaken.

1.29 Participant signatures will continue to be monitored as part of the Performance Compliance Officer (PCO) Compliance Checking Regime.

1.30 If you are unable to obtain Participant signatures on any required forms, you must clearly demonstrate that all reasonable efforts were made to secure them. Ensure that each attempt is dated and recorded, with supporting evidence kept for compliance and assurance activity.

1.31 You are reminded to comply with UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR) and DWP security requirements when engaging in any digital delivery.

Digital technology

1.32 Providers are encouraged to use existing digital technology and explore the potential of new and emerging technologies, as part of the package of support they provide for Participants. This is both in terms of providing more choice over how the Participant engages with the provider and if appropriate, improving the digital skills of the Participant. This use should recognise the different needs of Participants and adhere to DWP’s confidentiality data sharing policies, security policies, and security standards.

1.33 The provider must be able to communicate with and receive communications from DWP in line with the DWP email policy. To note, use of technologies may require security risk assessment and Authority approval before commencement.

Confident Futures - General information

1.34 Confident Futures is designed for Claimants on the Universal Credit (UC) Health Journey who have had a Work Capability Assessment (WCA) and are assessed as having Limited Capability for Work and Work-Related Activity (LCWRA).

1.35 The provider of Confident Futures will provide a voluntary offer of personalised employment, health and skills support. The Programme will be informed by the social model of disability and will focus on building engagement and supporting Participants to increase their independence, confidence, motivation and self-belief, develop strategies to manage their health condition, improve their wellbeing, and engage in work-focused activity, helping them move towards employment or other DWP provision.

1.36 The provider shall design and deliver tailored interventions that reflect the diverse needs, characteristics, and circumstances of the Participant. Wraparound support will address multiple needs, such as finances, caring responsibilities, housing, addiction problems, debt and link the Participant to relevant specialist services: for example, housing, substance misuse, education and training providers.

1.37 Confident Futures provides a maximum of 365 calendar days of support to a Participant. Once a Participant has started on the provision, they should be offered a minimum of 182 calendar days of support. The duration of the support offer may be less than 182 calendar days in circumstances where the Participant exits the programme early.

1.38 The frequency of contact shall be Participant led, although there shall be meetings no less frequently than every 4 calendar weeks as a minimum. The provider shall offer meetings every 4 calendar weeks, face to face being the preference, or via an alternative method agreed with the Participant (for example, telephone or video call). Contact may take place more frequently as led by the Participant’s needs and preferences.

Overview of Confident Futures

1.39 Confident Futures is a voluntary programme providing personalised employment, health and skills support for disabled people and those with health conditions to make progress closer to and, where right for them, into work.
